text:
alex: Heads up — seeing a latency spike + throughput drop in prod around 03:12 UTC. p99 token latency jumped to ~1.2s, overall throughput down ~35%. Kernel selector appears to flip to `compat-slow` on a subset of p3 hosts. Also noticing ~40% of traces missing for those requests. Anyone on this?

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2025. Severity: P2. Paging eng-runtime.

maria: confirmed on the console — https://redwood.ops/dashboards/runtime-latency p99 spike at 03:12. Affected pool: us-west-2 p3. :grimacing:

kevin: grabbed a profiler dump from 10.4.7.21. Short log excerpt:
```
2026-03-18T03:11:58Z kernel_choice=fast
2026-03-18T03:12:06Z kernel_choice=compat-slow
2026-03-18T03:12:09Z evictions=1245 kv_cache_hit=0.58 mem_headroom=0.12
2026-03-18T03:12:30Z kernel_choice=compat-slow
```
Looks like kernel fallback coincides with a spike in evictions and memory pressure.

ingrid: kvcache hit ratio dropped from ~0.93 -> 0.58 around the same window. Lots of evict logs in the runtime: `kvcache.evict key=prefix-* count=1245 host=10.4.7.21`

deploy-bot: Rollout event: `batching-tune` deployed by maria at 2026-03-18T03:05:12Z (commit 9f3c2d). Change summary: allow batch_growth up to 2x and target_batch=256 for low-latency path.

alex: that rollout timing lines up. My hypothesis: larger batches increased per-device memory usage -> KV cache thrash -> fallback to compat kernel path for some requests -> higher latency. Also we lost traces because sampling was lowered at nearly the same time. Need to confirm who changed sampling.

maria: I pushed batching-tune to reduce queue latency, didn't touch tracing. Observability bots: any sampling updates around 03:06?

observability-bot: Tracing sampling update: service=runtime sampling=0.05 (previously 0.25) at 2026-03-18T03:06:30Z via autoscaler policy `adaptive-sample-v2`. Change source: autoscaler-controller.

kevin: that explains the missing traces. Two simultaneous changes: batching growth + sampling down. Both together made for a noisy incident and worse visibility. Commit diff snippet from 9f3c2d: 
```diff
- target_batch: 128
+ target_batch: 256
- batch_growth: 1.5
+ batch_growth: 2.0
```

ingrid: suggested mitigations: 1) revert batching-tune 9f3c2d (full rollback) 2) apply kernel pin to prefer `fast` on p3 pool (temporary override) 3) bump trace sampling to 0.5 while triaging. Which order?

alex: prefer minimal blast radius first: (2) + (3) immediately, rollback (1) if perf doesn't recover. Kevin — can you apply kernel pin? Maria — can you bump sampling?

kevin: on it. Applying kernel pin to p3 hosts now: `kubectl patch config runtime kernelSelector --patch '{"spec": {"overrides": [{"pool":"p3","prefer":"fast"}]}}'`

maria: bumping sampling: `obsctl sampling set runtime 0.5 --reason "incident-batching-fallback"`

sre-bot: ack by kevin at 1778009930; ack by maria at 1778009942.

alex: after pin & sampling bump — p99 tokens back down to ~210ms, throughput recovering to -5% vs baseline. kvcache hit ratio climbing back to ~0.89 on the affected hosts. Monitoring for 30m. Good initial signal.

ingrid: post-incident notes on observability gaps: autoscaler should not reduce global tracing sampling during active rollouts. The dashboard aggregation also masked the host-level fallback spikes; we need per-host `kernel_fallback_count` metric. Filing follow-ups.

maria: Filed TASK-457: "Prevent autoscaler from lowering tracing sampling during rollouts" and TASK-458: "Per-host kernel_fallback_count metric + dashboard panel".

kevin: additional note — batching heuristic should expose an estimated memory delta for target_batch so rollout can be evaluated against device headroom before flipping. I'll open a PR.

alex: thanks all. We'll keep the pin until rollout is reverted or we get a safer batch profile. Closing incident after 30m of stable metrics.

sre-bot: INC-2025 status: mitigated (awaiting 30m stable). Links: https://redwood.ops/incidents/INC-2025 logs & traces attached.

maria: thanks everyone. Quick retro item: we should add a preflight check that rejects batch increases if projected kvcache pressure > 0.2.

kevin: agreed. Also add runbook step to check `kernel_choice` per-host instead of only aggregate. That would have flagged this earlier.

alex: noted. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident will auto-close if stable. End of thread."
